subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Biomimetic Materials: Copying Nature's Designs
description: A short lesson to help you apply Biomimetic Materials: Copying Nature's Designs.

hook.text: Gecko feet stick to glass without glue. A gecko can hang from one toe and support its full weight.

buildup.text: Millions of tiny hair-like structures create van der Waals forces. The attraction works on nearly any surface.

discovery.text: Engineers created Geckskin, an adhesive that holds 300 kilograms on a smooth wall using the same principle.

twist.text: Lotus leaves repel water with micro-bumps. Shark skin reduces drag with tiny ridges. Nature invented it first.

climax.text: Biomimetic materials now coat hospital walls, airplane wings, and swimsuits — all inspired by animals.

punchline.text: Nature had billions of years of R&D. Engineers just read the results.

quiz.question: What natural feature inspired the creation of Geckskin adhesive?
options: Spider silk's combination of strength and elasticity
Millions of tiny hair-like structures on gecko feet
The sticky mucus that snails leave behind on surfaces
